repo:objectstack#3 · os-support-ai · session_01WGufzgNCAXyGfBQFZBwixH

## Reading · 2026-11-17T20:44Z

**Answer in one line.** One authored rule refused 114 rows. The other 470 refused rows were children of those 114. The rule is sound and the card's seed is sound. The cause is the runner's seed path. It loads the card's rows through the ordinary data API, which applies the build's status state machine. The platform's own seed path skips that rule on purpose. A customer's first build does not meet this cause, so the card stays p2.

### 1. Which rule refused the rows

Source: the round's record `/mnt/project-files/issue-34687/ask-round-2026-11-17/build/travel_expense/2026-11-17-scenario-travel_expense.json`, field `cardRun.modes[0].run.seed.refused` (584 entries, `inserted: 173`). The Run half ran on dist `b7ab31a715d4e83c`. That dist is byte-identical to the `template.json` the ask, day1, five-rep and proof-managed runs replayed. Those five records show the same 173 inserted and 584 refused. So this is one build measured six times, not six builds.

| Object | Card rows | Refused | Code | Message | Kind |
|:---|---:|---:|:---|:---|:---|
| `expense_claim` | 120 | 114 | `VALIDATION_FAILED` | This status change is not allowed; a paid claim cannot be changed. | root |
| `claim_line` | 280 | 266 | `VALIDATION_FAILED` | Claim: no demotravel_expense_claim record has id "cNNN" | cascade |
| `approval_step` | 204 | 204 | `VALIDATION_FAILED` | Claim: no demotravel_expense_claim record has id "cNNN" | cascade |
| `department`, `employee`, `travel_standard`, `trip_request` | 153 | 0 | | | |
| **Total** | **757** | **584** | | | |

The refusing rule is the build's `claim_status_flow` on `demotravel_expense_claim`. It runs on `insert` and `update`:

```json
{"name":"claim_status_flow","type":"state_machine","field":"status","events":["insert","update"],
 "initialStates":["draft"],
 "transitions":{"draft":["submitted"],"submitted":["manager_approved","rejected"],"manager_approved":["finance_approved","rejected"],"finance_approved":["paid"],"rejected":["draft"],"paid":[]}}
```

`initialStates: ["draft"]` means a claim can only be created as `draft`. The card's seed holds 120 claims: 75 `paid`, 12 `rejected`, 12 `manager_approved`, 12 `submitted`, 3 `finance_approved` and 6 `draft`. Every non-draft claim was refused, which is 114. The 6 draft claims (c099, c100, c109, c110, c119, c120) went in. For example, row `expense_claim c001` is `{"status":"paid","paid_on":"2026-07-13", ...}`, and the insert check rejects it (`rule-validator.ts:3964`).

### 2. Where the cause lives

- **(c) The runner's seed path: yes, this is the cause.** `seedApp` sends each card row as `app.insertRow` ([orchestrate.ts:1192](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/blob/0465f4aa401f837ba1005a7986ff15a5fa74581b/packages/qa/scenarios/src/runner/orchestrate.ts#L1192)). That call is `POST /api/v1/data/OBJECT` with the admin's session ([app.ts:291](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/blob/0465f4aa401f837ba1005a7986ff15a5fa74581b/packages/qa/scenarios/src/runner/app.ts#L291)), so it counts as an ordinary user write, and the engine applies the state machine to it ([engine-insert.ts:1363](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/blob/0465f4aa401f837ba1005a7986ff15a5fa74581b/packages/objectql/src/engine-insert.ts#L1363)). The platform's own seed writers do something different. `AppPlugin` replays a stack's `data[]` ([app-plugin.ts:61](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/blob/0465f4aa401f837ba1005a7986ff15a5fa74581b/packages/runtime/src/app-plugin.ts#L61)), and `SeedLoaderService` and verify's `seed()` load seed rows. All of them write under `SEED_WRITE_EXECUTION_CONTEXT` (`seedReplay: true`, [execution-context.zod.ts:829](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/blob/0465f4aa401f837ba1005a7986ff15a5fa74581b/packages/spec/src/kernel/execution-context.zod.ts#L829)), which skips only the `state_machine` rule ([engine-top-level.ts:4088](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/blob/0465f4aa401f837ba1005a7986ff15a5fa74581b/packages/objectql/src/engine-top-level.ts#L4088)). The contract says why: without the exemption, a declared `initialStates` "silently rejects every mid-lifecycle seed row (and cascades its master-detail children)" ([execution-context.zod.ts:650-672](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/blob/0465f4aa401f837ba1005a7986ff15a5fa74581b/packages/spec/src/kernel/execution-context.zod.ts#L650-L672)). That is exactly what this round recorded. The card's rows are established facts, but the runner loads them through the door meant for new records. Neither the runner nor its README mentions state machines, `initialStates` or `seedReplay` (zero hits in `packages/qa/scenarios/**` and `.claude/skills/scenario-eval/**`). The README even states the door: "rows go in as the admin" (README.md:485). The restore path uses the same door too (orchestrate.ts:1383).
- **(b) The skill: it taught the rule, but the teaching is correct.** `skills/objectstack-data/SKILL.md:333` says a `state_machine` "also declares `initialStates` whenever the status has a real starting point — without it a record can be created already `approved` / `paid`". `rules/validation.md:18` and `:109` say the same. The author transcript (`scratch.rec.json`) reads that passage before it writes `initialStates: ['draft']`. The card prompt asks for it as well: "a payment cannot be undone". That is the right design for a real app, so the skill should not change.
- **(a) The card's seed: no contradiction.** I replayed the build's own declarative rules over all 757 card rows, using `evaluateValidationRules` from `packages/objectql` at `0465f4aa40` with the build's `template.json`. With the state machine applied: 114 refused, all of them `claim_status_flow`. Every `claim_line` and `approval_step` row passes its own rules (`over_standard_needs_reason`, `decided_on` requiredWhen). Every paid claim carries `paid_on`, and every trip passes `end_after_start`. With `skipStateMachine: true` (the seed posture): **0 of 757 refused**. This replay covers the rule layer only, not lookups, permissions or hooks.
- **(d) The platform: not a defect.** Refusing a non-draft create through the data API is the documented behaviour. An administrator cannot opt out over HTTP either: `treatAsHistorical` is refused from every caller except the system principal ([export.zod.ts:334](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/blob/0465f4aa401f837ba1005a7986ff15a5fa74581b/packages/spec/src/api/export.zod.ts#L334)). That is a design decision, not a bug.

### 3. Root and cascade

There are 114 root refusals, all on `expense_claim` from `claim_status_flow`. There are 470 cascaded refusals: 266 `claim_line` and 204 `approval_step`. Each one failed the lookup check because its parent claim was never inserted. Their own rules pass, as the replay above shows. No department, employee, trip or standard was refused. What the round lost: 8 question turns and 3 operations were not measured, and the guardrail `injection_as_data` was not measured either (its row `as_013_1` is a cascaded step).

### 4. Would a customer's first build meet it?

**No.** The build is right to declare `initialStates`. A customer's demo or bootstrap data, declared as `data[]` or `defineSeed`, loads under `seedReplay` and skips the rule by design (#3433). Records a customer's users create start as `draft`, as they should. The one customer path that meets the same refusal is importing historical mid-lifecycle claims as a signed-in user. That is a separate, deliberate boundary (`treatAsHistorical` is system-only), not this defect. So I do not recommend raising the card to p1.

### 5. The smallest fix and where it lives

The fix belongs in the runner (`packages/qa/scenarios/src/runner/**`), not in the card and not in `skills/**`, so it is not Tier H. The runner should load `run.seed` the way the platform loads seed data, under the seed write posture. One route, to be confirmed when the fix is claimed: emit the card's rows as the booted stack's declared `data[]`, so `AppPlugin` replays them with `SEED_WRITE_EXECUTION_CONTEXT`. Whether `data[]` keeps the card's own `id` values as lookup targets has not been checked yet. Then keep the runner's existing second pass only for what needs runtime ids: `owner_id`, the persona `user` field, the user-handle rewrites and the deferred cycle lookups. Those updates leave `status` unset, so the state machine never checks them (`rules/validation.md:18`: judged "only when the write sets the field"). Template and ask modes need the same rows carried with the install. `restoreSeededRows` (orchestrate.ts:1383) needs the same posture when it re-inserts a seeded row.

A side effect: seed replay also skips record triggers. The runner's current inserts fire them. The card's truths are computed over the seed rows alone, so skipping triggers is closer to what the card measures. Still, the scorecard should report the change.

I rejected two alternatives. Walking each row through the build's transitions fires flows on every step and depends on each build's own rules. Telling builds through the data contract (prompts.ts:430) not to declare `initialStates` would teach them to weaken the app.

Evidence: `/mnt/project-files/issue-34687/ask-round-2026-11-17/build/travel_expense/` (record, `template.json`, `scratch.rec.json`). The replay was a 30-line `tsx` script calling `evaluateValidationRules(schema, row, 'insert', { skipStateMachine })` for each card row. It was not kept. No code, branch or PR came from this reading.

## Delivered · 2026-11-18T00:48Z

PR #34985 merged to `main` at `4df62e6e0d` and closed this card (`Fixes`). The scenario runner now loads a card's `run.seed` rows as a data-only package's declared `data[]` through the harness's managed install door. That means they are written under the platform's seed posture (`SEED_WRITE_EXECUTION_CONTEXT`): a build's `state_machine` `initialStates` no longer refuses mid-lifecycle seed rows, while every other rule and hook still judges each row. `restoreSeededRows` takes the same path. Persona user ids ride in the load, and the second pass sets only the deferred cycle lookups (seat ruling A, 21:58Z). Refused rows are still recorded, now with the loader's sentence and no code.

Seat conditions:
1. The card ids stay lookup targets.
2. The README and the changeset say seed rows no longer fire record-triggered flows, and no card relied on it.
3. The kept `travel_expense` build replays with 757 inserted and 0 refused, so 0 of the 114 root refusals remain and the 470 cascaded rows go in (`/mnt/project-files/issue-34897/rerun-replay/`).

Reviews: L1-c ACCEPT 6962248251, delta ACCEPT 6962781877, and merge-only ACCEPT 6964373778. `pm:dispatched` and `lease:o3-G` removed in this stroke.
